How to use this book

PURPOSE, USE & DOCUMENTS
READ THIS PAGE FIRST
Purpose · what this book governs

The brand identity manual for The Imperial Culture: who we are, what we stand for, and how the brand is presented consistently at every touchpoint.

Think of it as the single source of truth. When a question about the brand comes up, the answer lives here. Where a page conflicts with a newer approved decision, the record wins and this book is revised. The book is never overruled silently.

The rules of use
Nothing ships off-system: colour, type, spacing and grid come from Visual identity (2.3), never reinvented per artwork
The wordmark is never redrawn, recoloured or rebuilt: assets come from Documents (4.1)
Confidential: internal teams and authorised partners only, see Terms (1.0) and Legal (4.2)
Nothing public without sign-off: the approval path in Governance (4.3) closes every release
Reading this book · the system is modular
Start with strategy

Part 1 to 2.1 explain the thinking. Read them once so every later decision stays anchored.

Learn the identity

Parts 2.2 and 2.3 are the working reference: voice, logo, colour, type and elements.

Apply with confidence

Part 3 shows the brand in the real world. Match new work to the closest example.

Protect and approve

Part 4 governs files, legal use, collaboration and sign-off before anything ships.

Brand OS v2.0 · The Imperial Culture© 2026 The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd.4
Terms &
Conditions
Important notice

This book is confidential. It circulates to The Imperial Culture staff and authorised partners only, and every copy remains the property of The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd. Access ends when a role or engagement ends, and copies are returned or destroyed on request.

Ownership

The name, marks, colour system, typography and visual signatures belong to The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd. The system is governed through the brand custodian. No period of use, however long, transfers any right in the marks or the masters.

Alterations

Masters are never modified. Refinement requests travel through the approval chain (4.3); a working copy is never the source of truth. When a rule blocks real work, the rule is raised and revised, never quietly bent.

Distribution

Files come from Documents (4.1), versioned, via the brand custodian. Forwarded copies and re-exports fall outside the system and are withdrawn. If a file did not come from Documents, it does not speak for the brand.

Permitted use

Use this book to produce on-brand work for The Imperial Culture. Nothing here may be republished, resold or supplied to a third party without sign-off. Work made inside these rules needs no further approval; anything outside them routes through the brand custodian first.

Confidentiality

Recipes, unreleased flavours, supplier detail and commercial figures stay out of anything produced from this book. What the brand has not published, the brand does not publish, in any market and on any surface.

Claims

Every health, function and labelling claim clears Legal (4.2) before publication, in each market it appears in. A credential seal is applied only where it has been cleared for that market.

Acceptance

Using any part of this system is acceptance of these terms. Exceptions are decided in Governance (4.3), not improvised. A recorded sign-off in that chain is the only path around any rule here.

Validity

This book is Brand OS v2.0. It stands until a versioned successor replaces it in Documents, and the newest master there is the only valid copy. A printed or exported copy is a snapshot, not the system.

Company introduction

WHO WE ARE
LIVING CULTURE KOMBUCHA
What The Imperial Culture is

The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd. is a living culture kombucha maker: small-batch, slow-brewed, and genuinely alive.

We brew for modern, health-aware people who value quality and ritual, and we exist to make wellness feel like a pleasure, not a chore. Real fermentation, real function, no compromise.

The double meaning · locked
In the bottle

The living culture

The ferment doing quiet work: live, raw and unfiltered, and the reason the drink tastes the way it does.

In the name

Culture as a way of living

Taste, refinement and intention. The everyday ritual, made worth slowing down for.

2.1 · Who we are

Our story

THE NAME, THE DOUBLE MEANING
CULTURE, TWICE OVER
Time is the ingredientFig. 2.1b

A brand born
from patience

The Imperial Culture began with a simple idea: the best things are not rushed. Kombucha is proof, a drink that only becomes itself through time, care, and a living culture doing quiet work.

Our name carries the double meaning at the heart of the brand: culture as the living ferment that makes the drink alive, and culture as taste, refinement, and a way of living well.

2.1 · Who we are

Positioning & brand script

ABOVE FUNCTIONAL, BESIDE RITUAL
CRAFT IS THE COMPETITIVE EDGE
Where we stand

A premium living culture kombucha for modern people who take wellbeing seriously but refuse to make it joyless.

We sit above the functional, mass-produced end of the category, and beside the everyday rituals of people who care what they put into their bodies. We compete on craft and taste, never on price or volume.

CategoryLiving culture kombucha
TierPremium, craft, small batch
AudienceModern wellness generation
We are notMass, clinical, hype-led
Positioning statement

For the modern wellness generation, The Imperial Culture is the living culture kombucha that makes feeling good feel good, because real craft, real culture and real taste should never be a compromise.

Brand script

Culture takes time. We give it time, and what comes back is a drink that’s alive, bright, and good for you. This is your everyday ritual, refined.

The north star for taglines, captions and long-form copy: always warm, confident, unhurried.

2.1 · Who we are

Brand philosophy

THE BELIEF UNDER EVERYTHING
NOT LOUDER. WARMER.
Culture, cultivatedFig. 2.1c

Culture,
cultivated

We believe the things that are good for us should also feel good to us. Wellness has spent too long feeling like a discipline. We think it can feel like a pleasure.

So we design every part of the brand, the taste, the bottle, the words, the experience, to slow the moment down and make it feel more considered. Not louder. Warmer. More alive.

The Imperial Culture is about creating something people are glad to make part of their day, again and again.

Brand OS v2.0 · The Imperial Culture© 2026 The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd.18
2.2 · Verbal identity

How we communicate

THE WRITING STANDARD
PLAIN, GENEROUS, EDITED
✓  Do
Speak plainly and generously, as if sharing something good.
Be transparent about craft, ingredients and process.
Frame wellness as pleasure and ritual, not duty.
Edit ruthlessly: say more with less.
Bring warmth, lightness and a little effervescence.

Worked example. “Brewed slow and honest, bright on the tongue, kind to the gut.”

✕  Don’t
Oversell, exaggerate, or stack superlatives.
Make vague or unprovable health promises.
Shame, guilt or moralise about health.
Use filler, clichés or lazy buzzwords.
Sound flat, cold, corporate or clinical.

Off-brand example. “The #1 detox superdrink that finally fixes your gut, guaranteed!”

2.3 · Visual identity

Design principles

FOUR PRINCIPLES
THE PRINCIPLE OUTRANKS THE PREFERENCE

Four principles govern every design decision in this book. Where a layout is in doubt, the principle wins over the preference.

01

Warmth through light

Amber tones and soft light make every surface feel inviting and human, like golden hour, never cold.

02

Alive & effervescent

Bubbles, movement and living texture give the brand energy: bright, active, full of life.

03

Refined restraint

Premium is subtraction. Generous space, clean structure, one confident focal point. Nothing crowded.

04

Honest & natural

Real texture over gloss, real moments over staging. The craft is the story.

Visual identity · 2.3.1 Logo

Construction & clear space

THE X UNIT GOVERNS EVERYTHING
CLEARSPACE = X
XXXX
Built on a grid

X is the cap height of IMPERIAL CULTURE in the supplied lockup. Every measurement in the mark is a multiple of it, and minimum clearspace on all sides equals X: that zone stays free of type, imagery and competing elements.

In print, clearspace is never less than 5 mm on the sides or 10 mm top and bottom, whichever is larger.

The unit XCap height of IMPERIAL CULTURE
Lockup height2.97 X
Lockup width18.49 X · ratio 6.21 : 1
“THE” cap0.66 X · sits 0.39 X above
Tagline cap0.29 X · sits 0.64 X below
ClearspaceX on every side, all forms

No other element, type or image may enter the exclusion zone. When a layout cannot hold it, the layout changes, not the clearspace.

Colourways & backgrounds

FOUR COLOURWAYS · NO OTHERS
CONTRAST IS NOT NEGOTIABLE

Four approved colourways. Gold-on-ink and ink-on-cream are primary; everything else is a controlled exception.

Ink, on creamPRIMARY
Reversed white, on amberPRIMARY
Imperial Gold, on inkAPPROVED
Mono ink, single colourAPPROVED

Rule. Only place the logo on backgrounds that keep full contrast. On busy photography, use the reversed mark inside a solid brand block, never floating on the image.

Logo misuse

SIX WAYS TO BREAK IT
ALL SIX ARE FORBIDDEN

The logo’s integrity is the brand’s integrity. These rules are absolute, with no exceptions for any channel, partner or campaign.

✕Don’t distort

Never stretch, squash or skew.

✕Don’t recolour

Only the four approved colourways.

✕Don’t add effects

No shadows, glows or outlines.

✕Don’t reduce contrast

Never place on low-contrast grounds.

✕
THE IMPERIAL CULTUREThoughtfully Crafted
Don’t rebuild

Never re-type or re-space the lockup.

✕Don’t rotate

The lockup is always level.

Usage ratio · the identity

Visual identity · 2.3.2 Colour
Avoid
pairing !

These combinations compromise readability, contrast and balance. Gold on cream, ginger on cream and gold on amber all fall below the contrast floor.

Gold never carries a paragraph and never becomes a section background: it marks, it does not fill. A mark set on a gradient or a busy photograph loses its edge.

If a surface cannot hold an approved pairing, the surface is redesigned, not the palette. Nothing here is re-tinted to make a layout work.

SYSTEMDON’TS

2.3.8

Brand OS v2.0Pages 47 → 48
Visual identity · 2.3.8 Don’ts

System don’ts

SIX WAYS TO DILUTE IT
NONE OF THEM SHIP

Misuse is not only a logo problem. These are the six ways the wider system gets diluted, in order of how often it happens.

Colour

Gold as a page field, new tints, or off-palette accents.

Type

A third typeface, synthetic bold or italic, or a size off the ladder.

Layout

Crowded corners, competing focal points, or content outside the margins.

Imagery

Cold light, clinical staging, or the mark floating on a busy photograph.

Elements

Bubbles behind body copy, gradients under text, or a fourth element.

Tone

Discount-led shouting, health claims, or hype in any channel.

The check. If a piece of work would still be recognisable as ours with the logo removed, the system is working. If it needs the logo to be identifiable, something on this page has gone wrong.

Naming rules
Short, evocative, single or paired words (Golden Ginger, Wild Hibiscus).
Sensory and natural: reflect the ingredient or the feeling.
Consistent structure across the whole range.

Over-hyped or trend-chasing language.
Long, complex or hard-to-say names.

Brand OS v2.0Pages 70 → 72
4.2 · Legal

Legal, trademark & compliance

PROTECTED PROPERTY
CLAIMS CLEAR LEGAL FIRST

To preserve the integrity of The Imperial Culture, all brand elements are subject to legal protection and consistent, compliant use.

Intellectual property

The name, logo, wordmark, colour system, typography and visual signatures are protected property. They may not be reproduced, altered or extended without written approval.

Trademark usage

Use the registered mark consistently. Apply the appropriate symbol as advised by legal counsel, and never alter, redraw or recreate the mark for a single application.

Compliance

All product, health and labelling claims must meet local regulations. Route every wellness claim through legal review before publication, in every market.

Distinguish the trademark. Always use the full brand name as a distinctive brand, keep it consistent across all materials, and preserve its integrity to protect long-term brand value.

Brand OS v2.0 · The Imperial Culture© 2026 The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd.71
4.2 · Legal

Collaboration & co-branding

THREE POSTURES · ONE STANDARD
NEITHER BRAND CROWDS THE OTHER

Partnerships extend our reach, but never at the cost of our identity. When The Imperial Culture works with others, the brand leads with clarity, warmth and equal respect.

TIC leads

Curated collaborations and in-house editions. The Imperial Culture name takes primary position.

Equal partnership

Co-branded work. Clear, balanced lockups with defined spacing. Neither brand crowds the other.

Never

No cramped lockups, no colour compromise, no mixing of brand assets into a single mark.

The co-brand lockup
PARTNER
Equal lockup · divider = X, clearspace = X each sideApproved

Rule. Every partnership must protect the calm, premium character of the brand. If a collaboration would make TIC feel loud, cheap or off-tone, it is not the right partnership.

Brand OS v2.0Pages 73 → 75
4.3 · Governance

Protecting against dilution

THREE PRINCIPLES · FIVE RISKS
DILUTION IS CUMULATIVE
Core principles
01

Consistency over novelty

Repetition builds recognition. Resist constant reinvention.

02

Quality over volume

Never trade craft or premium feel for reach or speed.

03

Guard the tone

Avoid discount-led, hype or clinical messaging in every channel.

Dilution risks to watch
Aggressive discounting and “sale” messaging.
Off-brand colour, type or cluttered layouts.
Cheap materials or inconsistent packaging.
Overextending the range without structure.
Partnerships that clash with brand values.

The custodian’s question. Not “is this on brand?” but “if we did this every week for a year, what would the brand become?” Dilution is rarely one bad piece; it is a hundred small compromises.

Brand OS v2.0 · The Imperial Culture© 2026 The Imperial Culture Sdn. Bhd.74
4.3 · Governance

Approvals & sign-off

THREE STEPS · ONE CUSTODIAN
ONLY APPROVED WORK SHIPS

This guide upholds the brand’s integrity, but it cannot cover every case. When a new application is not answered here, route it through the brand custodian before it goes live.

Step 1

Create to guide

Match new work to the closest existing standard in this book.

→
Step 2

Submit for review

Send to the brand custodian with context: channel, market, run length.

→
Step 3

Approve & release

Only approved work ships, prints or publishes. No exceptions.

What always needs sign-off
All packaging and label artwork
Anything carrying a health or function claim
New product names and edition badging
Co-branded and partnership lockups
Out of home, press and paid media
Any new application not covered in this book
Turnaround

Allow three working days for standard review, and five for anything carrying a health or regulatory claim. Rush requests are accepted, but the standard is never lowered to meet a deadline.
